01
Executive verdict

The acquisition funnel is live. The game loop is not observable.

Physics-skill promise × real-stakes token economy × gated pre-launch world.

Observed The browser entry sells “a whole world to play for,” requires account verification, and then confirms the user is in—but explicitly says the gates will open soon. No hub, minigame selection, duel, physics interaction, wager setup, result or leaderboard data became accessible.

Best quality. Positioning is immediate. Pastel arcade-island art, oversized copy and three distinct entry actions make the fantasy and economy legible in seconds.

Main risk. The token funnel is actionable before the entertainment proof. New users can authenticate, buy, swap or inspect liquidity while the promised play surface remains unavailable, creating a severe trust and conversion inversion.

Study the funnel, not the unseen game

Product answer

The observed artifact is a prerelease landing/auth/economy shell. Any critique of physics quality, match fairness or duel retention would be fabricated.

Reconstruction answer

Reproduce only the visible landing, human-verification boundary, auth states, gated success state and safe external-token routes. Treat all gameplay screens as unknown.

03
What the product is

Publicly framed as an arcade world; observed as a waitlist-plus-token storefront.

Promised genre

Browser-based 1v1 physics skill duels and a shared Quip WRLD of minigames, leaderboards and real-stakes competition.

Observed product

Marketing landing page, human verification, Privy-powered login/sign-up, email-code verification, a gated “we’ll open the gates soon” state and external token-market links.

Fantasy

Enter a playful arcade island, prove mechanical skill, stake $PHYS and convert wins into payouts.

Current user goal

Create or connect an identity, secure early access, understand the $PHYS contract and choose whether to leave the site for an acquisition venue.

Target audience

Crypto-native competitive players comfortable with wallet identity, token markets and financialized skill contests. The email/SMS path broadens access beyond wallet-only users.

Availability boundary

Observed The prominent “Coming Soon · Quip WRLD” label and post-auth gate make the playable state unavailable in this route.

04
Observed first session

Verification succeeds; play does not begin.

The route ends before any gameplay. That absence is the central product fact, not a missing analytical step.

1 · Landing and proof-of-human

The initial viewport presents the WRLD pitch and token CTA while a Cloudflare human-verification widget overlays the lower-right corner.

2 · Account choice

“Log in or sign up” opens a centered Privy modal with email, SMS and wallet options. The island and pitch blur into a non-interactive backdrop.

3 · Email confirmation

The email route moves to a six-cell code form with back, close and resend. Verification completes successfully; sensitive account data is intentionally excluded from this report.

4 · Gated payoff

The landing card replaces login/create-account actions with “You’re in. We’ll open the gates soon.” The only remaining primary action is “Explore $PHYS.”

5 · External economy path

The token CTAs lead to external Jupiter and Solana Explorer surfaces. Market, liquidity, holder and contract details are visible; no wallet connection or transaction is performed.

6 · Furthest state

A public Solana token record is reached. No arcade island traversal, game list, duel queue, stake confirmation, result, payout or live leaderboard is observed.

05
Core loop

The only complete loop is acquisition, not play.

Read promise

Understand WRLD, real skill, real stakes and $PHYS.

Verify

Pass the human check and choose an identity route.

Authenticate

Complete email code, SMS or wallet flow.

Reach gate

Receive “You’re in” status but no playable destination.

Explore economy

Copy/view the contract or leave for buy, swap and pool destinations.

Unobserved gameplay loop

Radar describes “enter hub → choose duel/minigame → play skill challenge → compare result/leaderboard.” None of those states is visible in the captured product route. Reconstruction must not invent controls, physics, wager rules, matchmaking, settlement, anti-cheat or results.

08
Progression, economy and content

The economic layer is concrete; progression is only promised.

Current progression

Anonymous visitor → verified human → authenticated account → gated early-access status. No XP, level, rank, inventory or season progress is visible.

Currency

$PHYS is positioned as the utility token powering real-stakes play and payouts. The landing exposes contract identity and acquisition routes.

Price framing

The page advertises a genesis peg in USDC terms. External market data is dynamic and should not be treated as stable product copy.

Wagers & payouts

Unknown Minimum stake, rake/fees, escrow, refund, dispute, withdrawal and payout timing are not shown.

Content breadth

WRLD, multiple minigames, 1v1 duels and leaderboards are publicly claimed. No playable catalog, game card or content count is observed.

Expansion cost

Hypothesis High: each real-stakes minigame requires game design, deterministic/fair execution, matchmaking, settlement, fraud controls, compliance and live operations—not merely another arcade scene.

UX/UI reconstruction atlas

Five observed states define the current product.

The atlas documents the prerelease shell only. Gameplay canvas, lobby, queue, duel, wager and result screens remain outside the evidence boundary.

A · Landing / world promise

Purpose
Explain fantasy, establish $PHYS and route to identity or acquisition.
Composition
Full-bleed low-poly island; centered dark glass card around 38% viewport width; token section continues below fold.
Copy
“Coming Soon · Quip WRLD,” “A whole world to play for,” real skill / real stakes description.
Components
Log in, Create account, Explore $PHYS, contract address, Copy, Explorer, Buy, Swap, pool.
States
verification pending, unauthenticated, auth modal open, authenticated/gated.

B · Privy authentication modal

Purpose
Start or resume identity using a mainstream or crypto-native method.
Entry / exit
Log in / Create account; close restores landing.
Composition
White portrait dialog centered over strongly blurred world; compact heading; three full-width rows; provider credit at bottom.
Copy
“Log in or sign up,” email placeholder, “Continue with SMS,” “Continue with a wallet.”
States
idle, typing, submitting, provider error, verification step.
••••••

Email confirmation

Six-digit entry · Resend code · Back · Close

The original state was reviewed but its screenshot is intentionally omitted because it contains personal account information.

C · Verification code

Purpose
Prove control of the submitted email address.
Composition
Centered white dialog, envelope icon, explanatory copy, six visual cells, resend action and provider credit.
Interaction
Keyboard/paste input; auto-advance; back or close; resend.
States
empty, partial, complete/submitting, invalid, expired, resent, success (only empty and success path observed).
Privacy
Address must be masked in screenshots, logs and analytics.

D · Auth success / access gate

Purpose
Confirm identity and hold the user before release.
Copy
“You’re in. We’ll open the gates soon.” and “Explore $PHYS.”
Change
Log in / Create account disappear; no account chip, logout, game card or play CTA appears in the visible card.
Data
authenticated state, access entitlement/waitlist status (exact model unknown).
Risk
Success lacks next-step expectation, notification preference or release timing.

E · On-chain verification destination

Purpose
Let users inspect public token identity and transaction history.
Entry / exit
External explorer link; browser back/tab close returns.
Composition
Third-party dark data interface with token header, address, supply fields and history table.
Ownership
Not Quip UI. Treat as an external trust surface, not a screen to reproduce.
Unknown
Whether Quip validates destination/network mismatch or detects impersonation.

Typography

Oversized geometric/grotesk display face with very heavy weight; friendly rounded sans for body and actions; compact monospaced contract address. Exact families are unverified.

Shape language

18–28px card radii, 12–16px control radii, 2–5px dark borders, offset shadows and thick pill CTAs create toy-like physicality.

Responsive target

On narrow screens, keep headline first, stack auth buttons, wrap or truncate the address with a dedicated copy control, and keep financial disclosures above acquisition CTAs.

10
Feedback and presentation

Strong promotional feedback; thin completion feedback.

Visual identity

The island uses intentionally simple outlined geometry and candy color; the card adds glossy, high-contrast crypto-launch energy without losing the toy-world premise.

Modal focus

Heavy backdrop blur makes the active auth step unmistakable. White dialog, purple accents and large rows provide clear hierarchy.

Auth feedback

Method selection and code entry are structurally clear. The final success state is calm but provides no timing, notification or account-management detail.

Trust cues

Named auth provider, public contract, copy button and explorer link create verifiability. They do not substitute for gameplay proof, legal terms or risk explanation.

Motion & sound

Unknown No gameplay animation, physics feedback, haptics or sound was evidenced. The landing’s environmental motion was not established by still frames.

Error language

No invalid code, provider failure, wallet rejection, challenge failure or unavailable destination state was captured.

Promised return loops

13
Growth interpretation

Existing audience and real-stakes novelty likely drive more attention than proven gameplay.

Idea

Physics skill with real stakes is easy to debate and share. It combines competitive-game language with a financial outcome.

Visual hook

The low-poly island and giant “whole world” card create an immediately recognizable campaign asset.

Creator audience

Radar The official profile was recorded at 12.1K followers; a pinned Season 3 post had substantially larger historical engagement. Existing distribution is a plausible contributor.

Known IP

No established entertainment IP is identified. The Quip/$PHYS brand must generate its own recognition.

AI narrative

AI use is unknown in the source set. It should not be used to explain interest or development speed.

Counter-signal

Radar stored no independent origin and player count is unknown. The observed route cannot test whether social attention converts into play.

Interpretation. The strongest defensible explanation is a combination of existing account reach, provocative real-stakes positioning and a clear visual campaign. There is insufficient evidence for product-led growth, match retention or organic player advocacy.

Mandatory behavior

Availability truth

  • “Coming soon” remains visible before authentication.
  • Signup copy states that the result is gated access, not immediate play.
  • Post-auth state explains notification and release expectations.
  • Ads and metadata must use the same availability state.

Identity safety

  • Support email, SMS and wallet without privileged visual ranking.
  • Mask identifiers outside the active dialog.
  • Paste-friendly OTP with accessible single-code semantics.
  • Session, logout and wallet-disconnect controls once authenticated.

Financial boundary

  • Label all token actions as external and non-gameplay.
  • Show network/contract/risk context before leaving.
  • Never imply token purchase guarantees access or returns.
  • Do not render dynamic price as a fixed product promise.

Unknown game layer

  • Reserve route interfaces for hub, catalog, queue, match, result and leaderboard.
  • Do not implement wager/settlement semantics from marketing copy alone.
  • Require a future observed run before visual parity claims.
  • Keep game engine choice independent of landing stack.

17
Acceptance specification

Test the gate precisely; refuse to hallucinate the game.

1

First entry. Given an anonymous visitor, when the page loads, then the island, coming-soon label, headline, real-stakes/$PHYS description, auth CTAs, contract identity and token section are readable without horizontal overflow.

2

Human-check boundary. Given verification is required, when the widget is pending, then protected actions are unavailable without falsifying an account error; pass restores interaction, and provider failure offers a retry/support path.

3

Open auth. Given the landing is interactive, when Log in or Create account is activated, then the labeled modal traps focus, background controls become inert, and close restores focus to the triggering CTA.

4

Email verification. Given a valid email submission, when the six-digit code is pasted, then cells populate, one submit event occurs, and the identifier is masked outside the active dialog.

5

Invalid code. Given an expired or incorrect code, when verification completes, then an accessible error appears, entered digits can be corrected, resend respects cooldown and no gameplay entitlement is granted. Implementation choice; error screen not observed.

6

Auth success. Given successful verification but no active entitlement, when the modal closes, then the CTA row becomes “You’re in. We’ll open the gates soon,” Explore $PHYS remains available, and no Play button or accessible game route appears.

7

Contract copy. Given the verified Solana contract is displayed, when Copy is pressed, then the exact full address enters the clipboard and a text confirmation is announced without changing page position.

8

External token route. Given the user activates Buy, Swap, Pool or Explorer, then the named destination opens in a new tab after a clear external/risk disclosure; cancel leaves the page unchanged. Disclosure is a safety-oriented implementation choice.

9

Pause / resume. No game simulation exists in the observed build. Browser background/foreground transitions must preserve auth and scroll state; a fabricated pause menu must not be added.

10

Reset / logout. Given an authenticated gated account, when Logout is confirmed, then local session state clears and anonymous CTAs return; account deletion is a separate, explicitly scoped flow. Implementation choice; original controls unobserved.

11

Result screen. The only observed result is the gated success message. Match result, payout and leaderboard acceptance remain blocked until a completed match is directly observed.

12

Visual regression. At wide and narrow viewports, the island remains atmospheric, the pitch stays primary, auth rows remain at least 44px high, contract text never overlaps Copy, and financial disclosures remain adjacent to acquisition actions.

18
Experiments

Prove entertainment before optimizing token conversion.

No-stakes demo

Hypothesis
A 60-second practice challenge before auth will increase informed signup.
Test / metric
Demo vs current gate; demo completion, qualified signup, later first-match conversion.
False read risk
More signups may reflect novelty without willingness to play for stakes.

Expectation copy

Hypothesis
“Join the waitlist—play is not open yet” will reduce post-auth disappointment.
Test / metric
Explicit vs current CTA; auth completion, immediate exits, notification opt-in.
False read risk
Lower signup volume may represent healthier qualification, not failure.

Economy separation

Hypothesis
Moving buy/swap links behind an “Economy” explainer will improve trust without harming qualified intent.
Test / metric
Current layout vs separated module; comprehension, external clicks, complaints, return-to-site rate.
False read risk
Lower clicks can be either reduced confusion or reduced legitimate interest.

Release contract

Hypothesis
A dated access status and notification control will create a reason to return.
Test / metric
Generic gate vs milestone/status panel; opt-ins, repeat visits, release-day activation.
False read risk
Reminder clicks do not prove match retention.

Safety comprehension

Hypothesis
A short jurisdiction/risk/access checklist before external routes will reduce mistaken assumptions.
Test / metric
Checklist vs inline copy; comprehension questions, external continuation, support incidents.
False read risk
Reduced continuation may be the correct protection outcome.
19
Confidence and unknowns

High confidence in the pre-launch funnel; no evidence for gameplay reconstruction.

High confidence

  • Landing composition and exact main CTAs.
  • Coming-soon availability state.
  • Email, SMS and wallet auth choices.
  • Email-code path and gated success copy.
  • Contract, Buy, Jupiter and Meteora routes.
  • No match was reached in the observed route.

Medium confidence

  • Authenticated users are waitlisted rather than entitled.
  • $PHYS is intended for real-stakes duels/payouts.
  • WRLD expands an earlier 1v1 duel product.
  • The visible public contract is the canonical production contract.

Unknown

  • Games, controls, physics and scoring.
  • Matchmaking, wagers, escrow, fees and payout timing.
  • Leaderboard, seasons and anti-cheat.
  • Age/jurisdiction eligibility and responsible-play systems.
  • Team, engine, frontend, hosting and audits.
  • Mobile behavior, auth recovery and launch timing.

Evidence boundary

Observed Landing, security boundary, auth states, gated success and external financial routes come from direct product states. Radar Social counters, public timeline, profile context, Solana attribution and the advertised expansion from duels to WRLD come from the dated Radar snapshot and linked official source. Hypothesis Audience fit, expansion cost, trust effects and experiments are product interpretations. Unknown No unseen match or financial mechanism is asserted.

Bottom line. Quip’s visible shell is reconstruction-ready; Quip’s game is not. The next valid teardown step requires direct evidence of a safe no-transaction path through one full duel, its result, leaderboard update and any wager disclosure.
